channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Putin's Plane from Turkmenistan Lands in St. Petersburg Instead of Moscow Amid Drone Alerts
item.description: President Putin's aircraft, an Ilyushin Il-96 that flew to Turkmenistan, landed in St. Petersburg instead of Moscow on October 9. The plane later departed for the capital. The diversion may have been due to drone alerts, as Moscow airports briefly restricted flights.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Withhold Details on Payments to Families of Soldiers Lost at Sea
item.description: Kazakhstan will not disclose the amounts paid to families of military personnel who died or were injured during exercises in the Caspian Sea. This decision was made at the request of the families to ensure confidentiality. The commission has completed its work, and all funds have been distributed. Seventeen servicemen were lost at sea during exercises in September, with 14 fatalities.

item.title: Greek Company Plans to Process Metallurgical Waste in Kazakhstan
item.description: A Greek industrial group, Metlen Energy & Metals, plans to establish metallurgical waste processing in Kazakhstan to extract valuable metals like copper, zinc, and nickel. The project aligns with government priorities on waste recycling and value-added production. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed readiness to facilitate the project's development and cooperation with relevant ministries and companies.

item.title: US Temporarily Eases Sanctions on Russian Fuel to Lower Global Prices
item.description: The United States has temporarily eased sanctions on Russian fuel following an agreement for Russia to supply 300,000 tons of diesel to the global market. President Trump stated this decision aims to reduce rising diesel prices, which impact agriculture, heating, and transportation. The move comes ahead of midterm elections.

item.title: Iran Proposes New 'CIS+1' Format for Deeper Cooperation with Commonwealth States
item.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian proposed establishing a 'CIS+1' format to deepen Tehran's engagement with Commonwealth of Independent States members. Speaking at the CIS summit, he emphasized regional diplomacy's role in crisis resolution and conflict prevention. Iran sees itself as a bridge between Central Asia and open seas.

item.title: Gold Bars Worth $40 Million Confiscated at China Border, Smuggled by Kyrgyz Citizen
item.description: Kazakhstan's court confiscated six gold bars valued at 182.3 million tenge (approximately $40 million) that a citizen of Kyrgyzstan attempted to smuggle into China. The woman hid the bars, weighing 2.8 kilograms, under her shoe insoles. The gold, exceeding 99% purity, was seized at the Khorgos border crossing.

item.title: UAE Prosecutor General: Flydubai Co-pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack
item.description: The UAE's Prosecutor General announced that a Flydubai co-pilot intended to crash the plane into Ben Gurion Airport, inspired by the 9/11 attacks. Preliminary investigations suggest a pre-planned terrorist plot. The suspect had previously flown to Tel Aviv twice to familiarize himself with the route and airport before attempting the attack on a third flight.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Ex-Navy Commander Arrested, Citizens Recruited for Ukraine War
item.description: The former Commander of the Kazakh Navy has been arrested in connection with the deaths of 14 servicemen during exercises. Meanwhile, relatives of Kazakh citizens allegedly deceived into fighting in Ukraine have sought help from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The review also covers rising small business loan defaults and other key events.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Families Seek Return of Citizens Recruited for War, Military Probe Continues
item.description: Relatives of Kazakh citizens recruited for the war in Ukraine have appealed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for help. A probe into the Ministry of Defense following the Caspian Sea incident has led to 13 criminal cases. Kazakhstan citizens will receive basic medical care regardless of insurance status starting next year.

item.title: Former Head of Uzbekistan Migration Agency Appointed to New Role at 'Vatandoshlar' Foundation
item.description: Behzod Musaev, formerly leading Uzbekistan's Migration Agency, has been appointed chairman of the 'Vatandoshlar' public foundation. The foundation, established in 2021, fosters connections with and supports Uzbek citizens abroad. Musaev's dismissal from the agency in September followed corruption scandals, including allegations of involvement in illegal schemes for labor migration to South Korea.

item.title: Tajik National University Hosts Conference on Combating Corruption
item.description: A conference on the role of science and education in implementing state policy against corruption was held at Tajik National University on October 9, 2026. Organized by the Agency for State Financial Control and Anti-Corruption, the event gathered researchers, government officials, and students to discuss anti-corruption strategies and awareness.

item.title: New Textile Factory to Be Built in Turkestan Region by 2027 with Chinese Investment
item.description: A textile factory is planned for construction within the Turan special economic zone in Kazakhstan's Turkestan region, with an estimated investment of 15 billion tenge from a Chinese company. The facility is expected to be operational by July 2027, with project documentation currently being developed.

item.title: Norwegian Refugee Council: Kunar Earthquake Survivors Still Require Aid One Year Later
item.description: One year after a devastating earthquake in Kunar, survivors continue to need support, according to the Norwegian Refugee Council. Families require sustained assistance for rebuilding homes, accessing clean water, and restoring livelihoods. UN agencies report insufficient funding for disaster-affected populations, returning refugees, and displaced communities, exacerbating challenges from migration returns and unemployment.

item.title: Aidarbek Myrzakhmetov Appointed Minister of Defense
item.description: Aidarbek Myrzakhmetov has been appointed as the new Minister of Defense. Previously, he held the position of commander of the Special Operations Forces. This appointment marks a significant change in the country's military leadership.

item.title: Woman Arrested Attempting to Smuggle Gold Worth 182 Million Tenge into Kazakhstan
item.description: A citizen of Kyrgyzstan was apprehended attempting to smuggle gold worth 182 million tenge into China via Kazakhstan. Six gold bars, weighing 2.8 kg and with over 99% purity, were found hidden in the insoles of her shoes at the Khorgos border crossing. The gold was confiscated and transferred to state revenue.

item.title: Putin States Russia Ready to Supply Oil to US and Global Markets
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced Russia's readiness to supply oil to the US and global markets. The remarks followed a phone call with US counterpart Donald Trump, during which energy issues were discussed. This comes amid Western sanctions on Russia's oil industry due to the invasion of Ukraine, though Trump has introduced exemptions.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Inspect Over 46,000 Residential Properties in Four Days
item.description: During a four-day "Safe Home" operation in Kazakhstan, police inspected over 46,000 residential properties and checked more than 35,000 individuals. Approximately 4,000 individuals were found to be living without registration, and 3,000 violations were identified. The operation aims to prevent offenses and ensure public safety.

item.title: Uzbekistan Mandates Minimum Balance on Bank Cards After Loan Deductions
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has introduced new regulations requiring commercial banks to leave at least half of the minimum wage on customer bank cards after automatic loan or guarantee payments. This measure, effective from September 1, 2026, aims to ensure customers retain a minimum of 680,000 Uzbek soums on their cards if the minimum wage is set at 1.36 million soums.

item.title: Tajik and Iranian Presidents Meet in Turkmenistan on Sidelines of CIS Summit
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian held a meeting in the Avaza region of Turkmenistan on October 9. The meeting took place on the sidelines of the CIS Heads of State Council meeting. Rahmon welcomed Pezeshkian's participation, and discussions covered bilateral relations and cooperation.

item.title: Tokayev Appoints Commander for Kazakhstan's Special Operations Forces
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Sayat Isanov as the commander of the Special Operations Forces of the Armed Forces of Kazakhstan. Isanov, a lieutenant colonel, previously served as deputy commander. His responsibilities include overseeing combat, tactical, and airborne training for elite units. Details of his career were not publicly disclosed due to the nature of special forces service.

item.title: Gold Worth $182 Million Attempted to be Smuggled Out of Kazakhstan in Shoes
item.description: Six gold bars, valued at 182.3 million tenge (approximately $400,000 USD), were seized after a citizen of Kyrgyzstan attempted to smuggle them into China hidden in shoe insoles. The gold, purchased in Kyrgyzstan and brought into Kazakhstan, was discovered at the Khorgos border crossing. The bars, weighing 2.8 kg, contained over 99% pure gold.

item.title: US President Trump and Russian President Putin Discussed Easing Sanctions and Diesel Exports
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone call on October 9th. They agreed on Russian diesel fuel supplies to the US and global markets. Trump described the talks as 'very successful.' The leaders also discussed the Ukraine crisis and bilateral relations.

item.title: China and EU Release Joint Statement Following Second Session of Trade and Investment Conference
item.description: China's Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and EU Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič held the second session of the China-EU trade and investment meeting in Beijing. They agreed on outcomes in trade balance, export controls, intellectual property, and WTO reform. Discussions included potential tariff reductions and EU investigations into Chinese electric vehicles.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Commander for Special Operations Forces
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Sayat Serikqazyuly Isanov as the new Commander of the Special Operations Forces of the Armed Forces. This follows the recent appointment of Aidoss Sakenuly Myrzakhmetov as the Minister of Defense. The President had previously tasked the new minister with strengthening security within the military and emphasized the need for better equipment for soldiers.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Appoints New Commander for Special Operations Forces
item.description: Kazakhstani President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Sayat Isanov as the new Commander of the Special Operations Forces of the Armed Forces. The command was established in January 2022. Previously, Aidos Myrzakhmetov held this position before being appointed Minister of Defense on September 27, 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Launch System for Advance Notification of Planned Power Outages
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to implement a system to notify electricity consumers one to two days in advance about planned power outages. The head of 'Hududiy elektr tarmoqlari', Sardor Iskulov, stated that complete elimination of power disruptions is impossible due to potential accidents and the necessity of repairs and modernization. The new system will utilize Telegram for notifications.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Declares Caspian Sea Issue an Economic Crisis, Not Just Environmental
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has stated that the problems surrounding the Caspian Sea have escalated beyond an environmental crisis to become a significant economic concern. He emphasized the growing economic implications of the situation in the Caspian region.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Highlights CIS as Platform for Political Dialogue and Security Cooperation
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon stated that the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) has proven its value over 35 years as a platform for political dialogue, economic and humanitarian ties, and security cooperation. He noted the robust legal framework within the CIS and its adaptation to new realities.

item.title: Russian Diesel Returns to US Market Following Talks Between Trump and Putin
item.description: Russian diesel is set to re-enter the US market after discussions between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. Washington has also temporarily eased sanctions on Russian diesel. The President of Ukraine described this decision as an "investment in war."

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Smartphone Verification Rules via Digital Government Portal
item.description: Kazakhstan has updated its smartphone verification procedures. Physical individuals can now only verify their devices through the Digital Government portal and the eGov Mobile application. The new process includes automatic data retrieval and mandatory video identification to enhance personal data protection, simplifying user procedures and strengthening security.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Nurlan Dombaev Wins Historic Gold in Para Taekwondo Grand Prix
item.description: Kazakh athlete Nurlan Dombaev secured a historic gold medal in the 80kg (K44) category at the Para Taekwondo Grand Prix in France, defeating Brazil's Joel Gomes da Silva in the final. This marks the first Grand Prix gold for Kazakhstan in para taekwondo. Dombaev is a two-time world champion and previously won bronze at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games.

item.title: Pakistan Rejects Afghan Allegations of Links to ISKP Amid Rising Tensions
item.description: Pakistan's Foreign Ministry has rejected Afghan Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi's allegations of Islamabad's links to the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP). The spokesperson stated that the Islamic Emirate administration is responsible for security in Afghanistan's Badakhshan and Nuristan provinces and claimed that TTP and BLA operate from Afghan safe havens. Pakistan defended its military strikes as targeted.

item.title: 150 Kazakh Athletes to Compete in the 5th Asian Para Games in Japan
item.description: Kazakhstan will send 150 athletes to compete in 12 sports at the 5th Asian Para Games in Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, Japan, from October 18-24. The national team will participate in seated volleyball, para taekwondo, para judo, para table tennis, para shooting, para athletics, para archery, para swimming, wheelchair tennis, para powerlifting, boccia, and para cycling. Wheelchair tennis and para athletics for athletes with intellectual impairments will debut for Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstani Citizen Accused of Espionage for Ukraine and Supporting Extremism in Russia
item.description: Roman Belov, a citizen of Kazakhstan, faces charges in Russia for allegedly spying for Ukraine and supporting extremism. Russia's FSB completed its investigation. Human rights advocates report that Kazakhstani diplomats were denied access to Belov, who claims he was deceived and beaten after arriving in Orenburg.

item.title: Kazakhstan Shares Interpol Cooperation Experience at International Meeting in Astana
item.description: Astana hosted a meeting of Interpol National Central Bureau heads from eight countries, focusing on combating transnational crime, international wanted lists, and cyber threats. Kazakhstan presented its experience using Interpol's tools and databases. The Regional Action Plan for Central Asia was also discussed.

item.title: New International Terminal to Be Built at Dushanbe Airport
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has laid the foundation stone for a new international terminal at Dushanbe Airport. The project, aiming for modern international standards, will have a capacity of 8.5 million passengers annually and is expected to be completed in 18 months.

item.title: Taliban Justice Minister Accused of Detaining Residents to Force Rent Payments
item.description: The Taliban's justice minister, Abdul Hakim Sharae, is reportedly operating a prison within the ministry to detain residents of Omid Sabz Township. Sources claim he is forcing them to pay rent or vacate their homes. Dozens have allegedly been imprisoned over the past month for refusing to comply with the rent demands.

item.title: US, Ukraine, and Europe Negotiate Potential End to Ukraine-Russia War
item.description: Representatives from the United States, Ukraine, and Europe held discussions in Miami regarding a potential end to the conflict between Ukraine and Russia. The US reportedly emphasized 'compromise' during the talks, which aimed to develop a unified plan to present to Russia before winter.

item.title: Kazakhstan Focuses on Developing Mugaljar Horse Breed for Global Brand Recognition
item.description: The "Sadagro" farm in Karkaraly is modernizing traditional horse breeding, focusing on the purebred Mugaljar horse. Established in 2020 and specializing in purebreds since 2021-2022, the farm aims to elevate the Kazakh horse breed into a global brand. The goal is to enhance the meat production qualities of this resilient local breed.

item.title: Taliban Recruiting Children for Military Service, Report Claims Dangerous Tasks
item.description: A report indicates that the Taliban is recruiting children for military service in Afghanistan. Minors are allegedly being used for dangerous tasks, including the placement of explosive devices. The report also states that children are being lured or forced into service from schools in Pakistan.
